drug_class: Topical corticosteroid (medium-to-high potency steroid cream or ointment)
purpose: Prednicarbate is a prescription steroid cream or ointment used to relieve redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis, or allergic reactions. It helps calm the skin when it is inflamed or reacting. Your doctor may prescribe it for other skin conditions as well.
how_it_works: This medication works by reducing the activity of your immune system in the area where you apply it, which calms down inflammation and irritation. Think of it like turning down the volume on your skin's overactive response. It helps relieve itching, redness, and swelling by blocking the chemicals in your skin that cause those uncomfortable symptoms.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or itching right where you apply it, especially at first. You may also notice skin dryness, thinning of the skin with long-term use, or small stretch marks. Some people notice the treated area becomes slightly lighter in color over time.
warnings: Do not use this cream on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as the skin is thinner in those areas and absorbs more medication. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or plastic wrap unless your doctor instructs you to. Do not use it near your eyes. Long-term use or use over large areas of skin can affect your body's natural hormone levels, especially in children. Always use the smallest amount needed for the shortest time possible.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area once or twice a day, as directed by your doctor. Gently rub it in until it disappears into the skin. Do not use more than prescribed, and do not use it for longer than your doctor recommends — usually no more than 2 to 4 weeks without re-evaluation.
